## Bug Fixes

- Preserve `SYSTEMROOT`, `TEMP`, and `TMP` when launching remote stdio MCP servers with explicitly configured remote environment variables, allowing Unix hosts to retain the Windows executor's startup environment.

## Changelog

- [#51121](https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/51121): Backport Windows remote MCP environment preservation to 0.160.

prs.title: Gate Guardian continuation tests on classifier request capture
Honor prior cancellation before starting Codex delegates
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Honor prior cancellation before starting Codex delegates

## Why

An already-cancelled delegate spawn can report a runtime admission or startup error instead of `TurnAborted`, including when runtime shutdown has been requested.

## What changed

Check the cancellation token before runtime admission and session startup so prior cancellation returns `TurnAborted` immediately after approval-policy validation.

## Testing

Extend the pre-cancelled spawn test to cover both normal operation and requested runtime shutdown, asserting `TurnAborted` within a one-second timeout.

prs.title: Ignore stale refresh responses in agents overview tests
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Ignore stale refresh responses in agents overview tests

## Why

Aborting a refresh task cannot retract a response already queued for delivery. The test helper could consume that stale response and return before the replacement refresh completed.

## What changed

Make `finish_overview_refresh` skip responses whose request ID does not match the active refresh. Extend the lifecycle test to queue an invalidated response before removing a task, exercising the wait for the replacement refresh.

prs.title: Scope Guardian V2 response timing to snapshot sampling
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Scope Guardian V2 response timing to snapshot sampling

## What changed

Measure `responses_duration` directly around `sampler.sample()` in the snapshot classification path. Leave it unset for conversation classification instead of timing submission and waiting for the score.

prs.title: Use issuing-step context for Guardian MCP elicitation reviews
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Use issuing-step context for Guardian MCP elicitation reviews

## Why

MCP elicitation reviews used turn-start context, which could omit remote environments that became ready before the tool invocation and use stale environment permissions.

## What changed

Capture the issuing step's Guardian review context with each live MCP invocation and reuse it for elicitation reviews. Fall back to turn context when no matching live invocation is available, and preserve the captured context for in-flight actions.

## Testing

Extend the deferred-executor regression test to cover MCP elicitations, checking that Guardian receives the newly ready remote environment and its denied paths, excludes stale local denied paths, and returns the denial to the parent model.

prs.title: Preserve trusted-tool context in Guardian Decisions requests
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Preserve trusted-tool context in Guardian Decisions requests

## Why

The Decisions adapter rejected developer messages, including host-annotated trusted-tool context. Requests containing that context could not be classified.

## What changed

Append developer text annotated with `TrustedTool::KIND` to the classification rubric, preserving its authority while keeping user evidence in the input messages. Accept only a single text part with a single matching annotation; continue rejecting other developer messages and unsupported evidence.

## Testing

Add a regression test covering trusted-tool context alongside untrusted user text, plus rejection of incorrect roles, missing or mismatched annotations, multiple annotations or content parts, and image content.

prs.title: Install full context in compaction replacement history
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Install full context in compaction replacement history

## Why

Manual, pre-turn, and post-turn compaction previously deferred rebuilding initial context until the next turn. Their saved replacement history could omit refreshed instructions and skill catalogs.

## What changed

- Install initial context during local and remote compaction, before the last real user message or summary, keeping the compaction summary last.
- Persist matching full world-state and turn-context baselines with every replacement instead of retaining only partial extension metadata.
- Build replacement context and recompute token usage for the current model even when the previous model performs compaction. Reuse that captured context for eligible current-model retries.
- Capture manual compaction context centrally and propagate preparation errors to the task runner.

## Testing

Update assertions and snapshots for context ordering, refreshed instructions, resume and fork history, current-model checkpoint baselines, and cloud skill catalog retention across compaction and resume.

prs.title: Clarify incremental tool namespace updates in Responses Lite
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Clarify incremental tool namespace updates in Responses Lite

## Why

Incremental namespace declarations contain only changed or added tools. Their descriptions need to make clear that previously declared tools remain available unless explicitly marked unavailable, and that redefinitions replace earlier definitions.

## What changed

Append this guidance to updates of existing namespaces, preserving any namespace description. Leave initial declarations and catalog hashes unchanged.

## Testing

Extend unit and request-history coverage for the namespace hint, unchanged turns that append no tool definitions, and MCP tool removals that append a standalone notice without rewriting history or repeating the notice on the next turn.

prs.title: Add promise settlement streaming helpers to code mode
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Add promise settlement streaming helpers to code mode

## What changed

Expose two JavaScript globals for consuming results as inputs settle:

- `as_settled(promises)` returns an async iterator of fulfilled and rejected records in settlement order, preserving queued results while the consumer is busy.
- `stream_settled(promises, emit)` delivers those records to a callback, awaiting each invocation and propagating callback errors.

Records include an `index`, a `status`, and either a `value` or a `reason`. Iterable inputs use positional indices; `Map` inputs retain their keys. Both helpers accept promises, thenables, and plain values.

## Testing

Add runtime coverage for ordering, input types, object identity, callback behavior, early iteration exit, and termination. Add stdio and gRPC host tests for partial results across waits, plus a scenario snapshot verifying fulfilled and rejected records reach the model.

prs.title: Allow Guardian Decisions to fall back to `OPENAI_API_KEY`
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Allow Guardian Decisions to fall back to `OPENAI_API_KEY`

## What changed

Use `OPENAI_API_KEY` for the Guardian Decisions sampler when `CODEX_GUARDIAN_DECISIONS_API_KEY` is absent, the provider is `openai`, and no custom base URL is configured. Preserve dedicated-key precedence, including empty values, and do not fall back for other providers or custom base URLs.

## Testing

Add a credential-selection test covering fallback, dedicated-key precedence, empty dedicated keys, and provider and base URL restrictions.

prs.title: Recover Guardian reviews from parent checkpoints
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Recover Guardian reviews from parent checkpoints

## Why

Reviewer compaction can invalidate previously admitted transcript evidence. When a parent checkpoint is available, restarting from that checkpoint preserves the captured parent context instead of relying on a lossy reviewer summary.

## What changed

- Restart an invalidated reviewer once from the action-time parent checkpoint, within the original review deadline.
- Preserve fresh checkpoints during startup and fit review input using the existing budget selection.
- Select transcript evidence from the checkpoint actually loaded by the reviewer. Track the transcript source so cursors remain valid across legacy-history eviction and reset when the source changes.
- Resume transcript deltas after successful recovery, including authorization added after the parent checkpoint.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for checkpoint recovery, post-checkpoint authorization, resumed deltas, and stopping after one restart. Extend history tests to cover both legacy retention and parent-checkpoint reuse, and update the checkpoint-migration snapshot.

prs.title: Force fresh Guardian sessions for parent-checkpoint recovery
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Force fresh Guardian sessions for parent-checkpoint recovery

## Why

A Guardian review restarting from the parent checkpoint must bypass cached reviewer sessions and snapshots, even when another review is using the cached session.

## What changed

- Add `ReviewerRequest::requires_fresh_session` and enable it for parent-checkpoint recovery.
- Replace an idle cached session with a fresh reusable session, or start a fresh ephemeral session when the cached session is busy. Neither recovery path inherits a cached snapshot.
- Reserve the review permit before validating a cached session and before exposing a newly spawned session to concurrent requests.

## Testing

Add tests covering recovery with idle and busy cached sessions, verifying that recovery receives no cached snapshot and that subsequent reviews reuse the appropriate session.

prs.title: Isolate Guardian checkpoint recovery flags per review attempt
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Isolate Guardian checkpoint recovery flags per review attempt

## What changed

Give the initial Guardian review and its checkpoint recovery attempt separate recovery flags instead of resetting a shared flag. Keep the single restart under the original review deadline.

Represent reviewer selection explicitly with `ReuseIfAvailable` and `FreshParentCheckpoint`, so recovery requires a fresh session and ignores reusable fork snapshots.

prs.title: Send base instructions as Responses input messages
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Send base instructions as Responses input messages

## What changed

Move base instructions from the top-level `instructions` field into a prefixed `developer` message in `input` for standard Responses requests, matching Responses Lite. Remove the field from HTTP and WebSocket request types and assign instruction messages stable IDs derived from the thread and instruction text.

## Testing

Extend standard and Responses Lite tests to cover instruction message serialization, stable IDs, and resume consistency. Update WebSocket tests to verify that changed instructions trigger a full request without `previous_response_id`.

prs.title: Enforce required environment skills before model inference
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Enforce required environment skills before model inference

## What changed

- Accept per-environment `skills.required` lists through `environment/add` and `environments.toml`.
- Before inference, require each named skill to be enabled and supplied by the selected environment. Missing skills fail the turn before a model request, including when environment setup fails.
- Stop applying an environment's requirements after it is deselected. Exempt isolated Guardian reviewers, which have no skill catalog.

## Testing

Add tests for available, missing, disabled, and wrong-environment skills, failed environment setup, recovery after deselection, and propagation of TOML requirements to the correct environment.

prs.title: Sign the PowerShell installer in Windows releases
Remove obsolete Guardian thread-context enables from tests
Retry transient gRPC code-mode session admission failures
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Retry transient gRPC code-mode session admission failures

## Why

Transient admission errors or connection resets can prevent a code-mode session from opening before any execution starts.

## What changed

- Retry `OpenSession` and the initial lease message on `Unavailable` or `ResourceExhausted`, with at most three attempts and 100 ms and 200 ms delays within a single startup deadline.
- Classify HTTP connection and request failures as `Unavailable` so admission can recover from connection resets, while preserving error sources.
- Keep retries limited to initial admission so established executions are never replayed.

## Testing

Add gRPC integration tests covering transient status recovery, the retry limit, immediate failure for non-retryable statuses, and successful session execution after a connection reset.

prs.title: Prevent stable release pointers from moving backward
Record base instructions in incremental tool history
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Record base instructions in incremental tool history

## What changed

- Record nonempty base instructions as a developer message after tool declarations at the start of each incremental tool context window, and omit the request-level `instructions` field.
- Preserve this prefix when rebuilding history after local or remote compaction, while keeping the compaction summary last.
- Count recorded base instructions once when estimating context usage and trimming tool outputs.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for instruction placement, omission of request-level instructions, compaction ordering, and token accounting. Exercise remote compaction trimming with both request-level and recorded base instructions.

prs.title: Clean up Unix app-server control-socket startup lock files
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Clean up Unix app-server control-socket startup lock files

## Why

Unix control-socket shutdown removes the socket and rendezvous link but leaves the startup lock file behind.

## What changed

Keep a removable startup lock with the control-socket guard and release the lock after publishing the rendezvous link. On cleanup, reacquire the lock and verify that the path still identifies the same file before removing it.

Use nonblocking acquisition with asynchronous retries, checking file identity after acquisition to handle lock-file replacement.

## Testing

Add tests for nonblocking lock contention and dangling symlink rejection, and extend the control-socket lifecycle test to verify that the lock file is removed on shutdown.

prs.title: Wait for SIGCONT when resuming the TUI
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Wait for SIGCONT when resuming the TUI

## What changed

Install a temporary `SIGCONT` handler and unblock the signal during `Ctrl+Z` suspension. After sending `SIGTSTP`, wait for the handler to confirm resumption, returning a timeout error if no confirmation arrives within the bounded wait.

Restore the previous signal handler and thread signal mask, resume terminal stderr handling, and reapply terminal modes even when suspension fails. Propagate signal setup, delivery, and restoration errors to the caller.

prs.title: Test thread archiving before the first turn
Add browser extension request headers to config requirements
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Add browser extension request headers to config requirements

## What changed

Support `browser_use.extension.request_headers` as a list of `name`/`value` pairs and expose it through `config/requirements/read` as `browserUse.extension.requestHeaders`. Update the generated JSON schemas, TypeScript types, and Python models.

Preserve header values, including template strings, verbatim. Higher-priority requirement layers replace the entire header list, including with an explicit empty list. Redact header values in Rust debug output while retaining them in API serialization.

## Testing

Add coverage for parsing and malformed entries, extension scoping, empty-list overrides, API mapping and read responses, and debug redaction without changing serialized values.

prs.author: copyberry[bot]

prs.title: Distinguish namespace removals in incremental tool updates
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Distinguish namespace removals in incremental tool updates

## Why

Removing a whole namespace previously listed both the namespace and every member as unavailable tools.

## What changed

Emit separate namespace and individual-tool sections in one removal notice for Responses Lite. A removed namespace subsumes its members, with instructions allowing tools declared in a later update to become available again. Keep individual removal notices for tools in surviving namespaces and for built-ins.

## Testing

Expand unit tests and snapshots to cover mixed removals, empty catalogs, restoration, and replacing a namespace with a built-in of the same name. Extend the MCP refresh scenario to verify namespace removal and restoration, successful calls after restoration, preserved request history, and no repeated updates on unchanged turns.

prs.title: Make apply_patch preserve line endings unconditionally
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Make apply_patch preserve line endings unconditionally

## Why

Updating a CRLF file with `apply_patch` previously normalized its line endings to LF unless preservation was explicitly enabled. Preserve the file's existing line endings without requiring an opt-in.

## What changed

- Use line-ending-preserving updates for both tool calls and standalone `apply_patch` invocations, removing the legacy normalization mode.
- Mark `apply_patch_preserve_line_endings` as removed.
- Always set `CODEX_APPLY_PATCH_PRESERVE_LINE_ENDINGS=1` in child environments for compatibility with older patch executables, overriding stale values.

## Testing

Update CLI, tool-call, shell-heredoc, and app-server tests to check CRLF preservation by default. Keep coverage for overriding stale compatibility environment values.

prs.title: Record initialization analytics for resumed subagents
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Record initialization analytics for resumed subagents

## Why

Reloaded subagent threads did not emit initialization analytics, and subagent initialization events always reported `new`.

## What changed

Emit initialization events for resumed spawned subagents before notifying thread listeners. Inherit parent client metadata before reserving a residency slot can evict the parent, preserve the thread's original `created_at`, and report `initialization_mode` as `resumed`. Refresh stored analytics metadata when a subagent resumes; newly created subagents continue to report `new`.

## Testing

Extend the cold-resume integration test to verify a single worker initialization event with the expected session, parent, source, resume mode, and original creation timestamp. Update serialization and session tests to check initialization modes.

prs.title: Gate CLI Daybreak controls and selection behind an opt-in feature
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Gate CLI Daybreak controls and selection behind an opt-in feature

## What changed

Add `features.cli_daybreak`, disabled by default, to gate Daybreak controls and automatic access-program selection in the TUI and `codex exec`. Apply the gate to resumed sessions and background task turns, and hide `/daybreak` when disabled. Explicit `--cyber-access-program` overrides remain available.

## Testing

Extend tests to cover disabled controls, history replay, foreground and background turn requests, exec resume/fork behavior, and explicit access-program overrides with the feature disabled.

prs.title: Add ranked tool discovery to JavaScript code mode
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Add ranked tool discovery to JavaScript code mode

## What changed

- Add the default-disabled `code_mode_tool_search` feature to expose `await tools.tool_search({query: "...", limit: 8})` in code mode when the model supports tool search.
- Return BM25-ranked deferred tools as `{tools: [{name, description}]}`, including callable names and TypeScript declarations for use in later code cells.
- Filter results through the current step's nested-tool policy before applying the limit, preserving namespace restrictions, normalized identities, description prefixes, and schema budgets.
- Add ranked-search guidance while retaining `ALL_TOOLS` catalog discovery and description overrides.

## Testing

Add coverage for feature and model-capability gating, namespace restrictions, argument validation, schema budgets, and discovery followed by deferred MCP and dynamic tool calls. Extend the scenario snapshot to cover search, invocation, yielding, and completion through `wait`.

prs.title: Reject sandbox-writable bubblewrap executables from PATH
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Reject sandbox-writable bubblewrap executables from PATH

## Why

Bubblewrap discovery probes executables before confinement. Excluding only the command's current directory leaves candidates in other writable roots eligible to run outside the sandbox.

## What changed

- Filter canonical `PATH` candidates using the filesystem policy and effective user permissions, including writable ancestors, symlinked roots, and full-disk write access. Preserve protected system installations while rejecting replaceable paths.
- Select the launcher with the command's permissions before the proc-mount preflight, retaining the bundled bubblewrap fallback.
- Use the effective permission profile and policy working directory for startup warning probes.

## Testing

Add unit coverage for writable roots, symlinks, read-only carveouts, replaceable parents, and full-disk policies. Add Linux integration tests showing writable `bwrap` candidates are neither probed nor launched, including when the command runs in a workspace subdirectory or uses managed networking with full-disk write access.

prs.title: Measure raw MCP tool catalog sizes in telemetry
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Measure raw MCP tool catalog sizes in telemetry

## What changed

Record the total serialized JSON size of raw MCP tool definitions in the `codex.mcp.binding_catalog.raw_definition_json_bytes` histogram, before filtering or model preparation.

Emit an `mcp.binding_catalog` trace event for each server with its tool count, definition size, server kind, plugin ID, and cached or live catalog source. Reuse bounded product SKU attribution for both metrics and events, and skip size measurement when neither telemetry output is enabled.

prs.title: Preserve review targets and scope misalignment continuation metadata
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Preserve review targets and scope misalignment continuation metadata

## What changed

- Carry opaque `review_target` values through misalignment errors and expose optional `reviewTarget` in the app-server protocol and generated clients. Preserve the value verbatim and redact it from debug output.
- Keep target-based `misalignment_override` metadata on turn requests, preserve it across steering updates, and exclude it from compaction and external MCP metadata. Reject overrides from global Responses metadata while retaining legacy timestamp behavior for per-turn overrides.

## Testing

Extend coverage for error propagation, debug and rollout redaction, steering preservation, and metadata filtering. Verify that automatic compaction omits the review target while turn requests before and after compaction retain it.

Fix Windows 10 drive-letter opens for no-follow filesystem operations
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Fix Windows 10 drive-letter opens for no-follow filesystem operations

## Why

On Windows 10, strict native opens can reject the DOS drive alias itself as a reparse point, preventing no-follow filesystem operations on ordinary drive-letter paths.

## What changed

Retry rejected drive-letter opens relative to a verified local volume root. Require the root to resolve to a physical disk volume directory without reparse attributes, and retain `OBJ_DONT_REPARSE` for paths beneath it so junctions remain blocked.

## Testing

Add Windows tests for file creation and reading through the volume fallback, opening the drive root, and rejecting junction traversal and creation. Validate accepted volume-root names and verify that named pipes are rejected without establishing a client connection.
